method: Read existing artifacts and code only. Nothing was re-run.
question: Why is axis_px.start.x 266.0 while the drawing and the prediction continue farther left?

classification.split_with_another_upstream_segment: PARTLY: upstream wall_001 lies on the same line and ends at x 233.0, but a 33 px stretch between them belongs to no upstream wall

facts.fact: The endpoint is the vectorizer's value, copied unchanged. wall_002 centerline is [[266.0, 160.0417], [472.0, 160.0417]].
The region of interest did not cut the wall. It is computed from the selected walls after selection (x_min 228) and is used to filter aperture components and to frame the overlay.
Selection picks whole upstream walls by id and does not trim them. wall_001 was not selected.
Upstream wall_001 is on the same line: [[108.375, 160.0], [233.0, 160.0]], thickness 9.0. x 233.0 to 266.0 (33 px) is covered by no upstream wall.
The predicted mask is continuous there: on rows 157, 160 and 163 one run spans x 101..480. Its height is 9 px up to about x 237 and 8 px from about x 240.
No upstream intersection is recorded at x 233 or x 266. The nearest on this wall is (304.5, 160.04) with wall_012.
The vectorizer joins collinear segments only when they are at most 6 px apart, and Hough bridges gaps of at most 8 px. A 33 px gap is left as two walls.
Why no line was found between x 233 and 266 is not recorded. The vectorizer's skeleton and raw-line debug images were switched off for the bridge run.

unresolved: The cause of the 33 px gap, and so of the start at x 266.0. The existing evidence shows where the value came from and rules out a crop, but not why the vectorizer stopped there.
would_resolve_it: The vectorizer's skeleton and raw Hough lines for this mask. Producing them means re-running the vectorizer with debug output, which was not done because the request was limited to existing evidence.
consequence_for_review: The exported wall_002 is a part of the drawn wall, from x 266.0 to 472.0. Nothing marks it as a partial wall in the candidate geometry or the IFC.
